questions.solution: According to question, Let find slope of $A B, B C$ and $C A$ Slope of $A B=\frac{1-3}{1-(-2)}=\frac{-2}{3}$ Slope of $B C=\frac{3-\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)}{-2-0}=\frac{-2}{3}$ Slope of $C A=\frac{\frac{5}{3}-1}{0-1}=\frac{-2}{3}$ Since, slope of all lines are same, therefore, points are collinear.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The modulus of the complex number $z$ such that $|z+3-i|=1$ and $\arg (z)=\pi$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $z=x+i y$
Given, $\quad|z+3-i|=1\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad|(x+3)+(y-1) i|=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{(x+3)^2+(y-1)^2}=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad(x+3)^2+(y-1)^2=1\ldots(i)
\end{aligned}$
Above is the equation of circle with centre $\equiv(-3,1) and
\text{ radius }=1$
Also, $\arg (z)=\pi \Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left|\frac{y}{x}\right|=\pi\Rightarrow \quad\left|\frac{y}{x}\right|=\tan \pi=0 \Rightarrow y=0$

By Eq. (i),
$\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow & x & =-3 \\
\therefore & z & =-3+0 i \\
\Rightarrow & \text{ Modulus$ of $} z & =3
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $z, \bar{z},-z,-\bar{z}$ forms a rectangle of area $2 \sqrt{3}$ square units, then one such $z$ is
questions.solution: Let a complex number, $z=x+i y\Rightarrow \bar{z}=\bar{x}-i y$ Then, vertices of rectangle for $z, \bar{z},-z,-\bar{z}$ are $(x, y),(x,-y),(-x,-y),(-x, y)$ Now, Area of rectangle $=(2 x)(2 y)=4 x y$ It is given that, Area $=2 \sqrt{3}=4 x y \Rightarrow 2 x y=\sqrt{3}\therefore x=\frac{1}{2}, y=\sqrt{3} \quad \therefore z=\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{3} i$

questions.q: If $z_1, z_2, \ldots . . z_n$ are complex numbers such that $\left|z_1\right|=\left|z_2\right|=\ldots . .=\left|z_n\right|=1$, then $\left|z_1+z_2+\ldots . .+z_n\right|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\left|z_1\right|=\left|z_2\right|=\left|z_3\right|=\ldots \ldots .=\left|z_n\right|=1\Rightarrow z_1 \bar{z}_1=z_2 \bar{z}_2=z_3 \bar{z}_3=\ldots \ldots=z_n \bar{z}_n=1\overline{\mathrm{z}}_1=\frac{1}{\mathrm{z}}, \overline{\mathrm{z}}_2=\frac{1}{\mathrm{z}_2}, \overline{\mathrm{z}}_3=\frac{1}{\mathrm{z}_3}, \ldots \ldots, \overline{\mathrm{z}}_{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{z}_{\mathrm{n}}}$
Now, $\left|z_1+z_2+z_3+\ldots \ldots .+z_n\right|=\left|\bar{z}_1+\bar{z}_2+\ldots \ldots+\bar{z}_n\right|\left|\bar{z}_1+\bar{z}_2+\bar{z}_3+\ldots .+\bar{z}_n\right|=\left|\frac{1}{z_1}+\frac{1}{z_2}+\frac{1}{z_3}+\ldots \ldots+\frac{1}{z_n}\right|$

questions.solution: $\left|8 z_2 z_3+27 z_3 z_1+64 z_1 z_2\right|=\left|z_1\right|\left|z_2\right|\left|z_3\right|\left|\frac{8}{z_1}+\frac{27}{z_2}+\frac{64}{z_3}\right|=(2)(3)(4)\left|\frac{8 \bar{z}_1}{\left|z_1\right|^2}+\frac{27 \bar{z}_2}{\left|z_2\right|^2}+\frac{64 \bar{z}_3}{\left|z_3\right|^2}\right|=24\left|2 \bar{z}_1+3 \bar{z}_2+4 \bar{z}_3\right|=24\left|\overline{2 z_1+3 z_2+4 z_3}\right|=24\left|2 z_1+3 z_2+4 z_3\right|=(24)(4)=96$

questions.q: The modulus of $\frac{(1+i \sqrt{3})(2+2 i)}{(\sqrt{3}-i)}$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{(1+i \sqrt{3})(2+2 i)}{\sqrt{3}-i}=\frac{2+2 \sqrt{3} i+2 i-2 \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}-i} \\ & =\frac{(2-2 \sqrt{3})+(2 \sqrt{3}+2) i}{\sqrt{3}-i} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}+i}{\sqrt{3}+i} \\ & =\frac{2 \sqrt{3}-6+2 i-2 \sqrt{3} i+6 i+2 \sqrt{3} i-2 \sqrt{3}-2}{3+1} \\ & =\frac{8 i-8}{4}=-2+2 i \\ & \therefore \text{ Modulus }=\sqrt{(-2)^2+(2)^2}=2 \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The smallest positive integral value of $n$ such that 
$\left[\frac{1+\sin \frac{\pi}{8}+i \cos \frac{\pi}{8}}{1+\sin \frac{\pi}{8}-i \cos \frac{\pi}{8}}\right]^n$ is purely imaginary, is equal to
questions.solution:
$\left[\frac{1+\sin \frac{\pi}{8}+i \cos \frac{\pi}{8}}{1+\sin \frac{\pi}{8}-i \cos \frac{\pi}{8}}\right]^n=\left[\frac{1+\cos \alpha+i \sin \alpha}{1+\cos \alpha-i \sin \alpha}\right]^n\left[\because \alpha=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{8}\right]=\left[\frac{2 \cos ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2}+2 i \sin \frac{\alpha}{2} \cos \frac{\alpha}{2}}{2 \cos ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2}-2 i \sin \frac{\alpha}{2} \cos \frac{\alpha}{2}}\right]^n=\left[\frac{\cos \frac{\alpha}{2}+i \sin \frac{\alpha}{2}}{\cos \frac{\alpha}{2}-i \sin \frac{\alpha}{2}}\right]_{-}^n=\left(e^{2 i \frac{\alpha}{2}}\right]^n=e^{i n \alpha}=e^{i n\left(\frac{3 \pi}{8}\right)}=\cos \frac{3 n \pi}{8}+i \sin \frac{3 n \pi}{8}$
For $n=4$ we get imaginary part.

questions.q: If the real part of $\frac{\bar{z}+2}{\bar{z}-1}$ is $4, z \neq 1,$ then the locus of the point representing $z$ in the complex plane is
options: a straight line equally inclined to axes
questions.solution: Real part of $\frac{\bar{z}+2}{\bar{z}-1}$ is given by $\begin{array}{l}\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\bar{z}+2}{\bar{z}-1}+\left(\frac{\bar{z}+2}{\bar{z}-1}\right)\right]=$4 \\ \Rightarrow $\frac{\bar{z}+2}{\bar{z}-1}+\frac{z+2}{z-1}=$8 \\ \Rightarrow z \bar{z}-\bar{z}+2 z-2+z \bar{z}+2 \bar{z}-z-2 \\ =8(z \bar{z}-\bar{z}-z+1) \\ \Rightarrow z \bar{z}-$\frac{3}{2}$z-$\frac{3}{2} \bar{z}+$2=0 \end{array} Comparing with the equation $z \bar{z}+\bar{a} z+a \bar{z}+b=0,$ we get $a=-\frac{3}{2}$ and $b=2$. Thus, the locus of $z$ given by the equation (i) is a circle with centre $=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^{2}-x+1=0,$ then the equation whose roots are $\alpha^{100}$ and $\beta^{100}$ are
questions.solution: We have $x^{3}+1 \equiv(x+1)  \left(x^{2}-x+1\right)$. Therefore, \alphaand \betaare the complex cube roots of -1 so that we may take $\alpha=-\omegaand \beta=-\omega^{2},$ where $\omega \neq1$ is a cube root of unity. Thus $\alpha^{100}=(-\omega)^{100}=\omegaand \beta^{100}=\left(-\omega^{2}\right)^{100}=\omega^{2},$ so that the required equation is $\mathrmx^{2}+ \mathrm{x}+1=0$

questions.q: If $x=\omega-\omega^{2}-2,$ then the value of $x^{4}+3 x^{3}+2 x^{2}-11 x-6$ is
questions.solution: We have, $x=\omega-\omega^{2}-2$ or $x+2=\omega-\omega^{2}$ Squaring, $x^{2}+4 x+4=\omega^{2}+\omega^{4}-2 \omega^{3}=\omega^{2}+\omega^{3} \omega \cdot-2 \omega^{3}=\omega^{2}+\omega-2 \quad\left[\omega^{3}=1\right]=-1-2=-3 \Rightarrowx^{2}+4 x+7=0$ Dividing $x^{4}+3 x^{3}+2 x^{2}-11 x-6$ by $x^{2}+4 x+7$ we get $x^{4}+3 x^{3}+2 x^{2}-11 x-6=\left(x^{2}+4 x+7\right)\left(x^{2}-x-1\right)+1=(0)\left(\mathrmx^{2}-\mathrm{x}-1\right)+1=0+1=1$
